newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee costs will cause Bangor Hydro hike.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee costs will cause Bangor Hydro hike.

text.p: Costs associated with the continued shutdown of the Maine Yankee nuclear plant will cause Bangor Hydro-Electric Co to seek a rate hike and possibly review its dividend, the utility said.

In a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, the utility that owns seven percent of Maine Yankee said it would file a rate increase request soon with the Maine Public Utilities Commission (PUC).

The document filed Feb. 19, did not specify how much the hike request would be, but said any increase "would be held to a minimum." The utility had an informal agreement with the Maine PUC not to seek an increase until the year 2000.
The utility said while it believes a rate hike could cause long-term problems as the utility industry is deregulated, its "short-term need for greater revenue requires some form of increased rates."

Bangor Hydro said the uncertainty of its efforts to off-set Maine Yankee-related costs "increases the likelihood" its board will review the "sustainability of its current dividend payout." The board is scheduled to meet March 17.
